state: Site: JevCode (jevcode.ai), a Chinese-and-English bilingual aggregation site for Jev, the TypeSafe System One model. It aggregates: (1) translated official documentation from docs.typesafe.ai (concepts, primitives, patterns, SDK, API reference) in 8 languages (zh en ja ko de fr es pt); (2) cookbook-style case studies showing how to use Noul/Choice/Score question primitives in real pipelines (autoformat, rerank, guardrails, classification); (3) a community ecosystem index of GitHub projects using Jev, with star counts; (4) original analysis articles in Chinese about when to use judgment models vs generative models. Content count: 39 doc pages per language for zh and en, 20 for others with English fallback. The site is built with Astro static site generation. Current state: homepage is a hero plus card grids (primitives, patterns, quick links). Question: For a developer-facing documentation/aggregation site like this, what makes it GOOD vs mediocre from a content architecture standpoint? Evaluate these candidate directions: A) deeper original analysis articles vs B) staying a translation/aggregation hub; C) adding runnable interactive code examples; D) search functionality; E) comparison pages (Jev vs traditional LLM stacks). Give a verdict on which 2-3 directions to prioritize and why.

dir_analysis_articles.instructions: Is prioritizing deeper original analysis articles (original Chinese-language analysis of when to use judgment models) a high-value direction for this site?

criteria.true: High value: original analysis differentiates the site and attracts repeat visits
criteria.false: Low value: aggregation and translation already suffice, original analysis is not worth prioritizing
